dek: Every match streams live in the US as the race for a new European champion begins.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: The *UEFA Champions League* returns for 2026/27, Europe's top club soccer competition.

slides.label: Who's chasing history
slides.text: Two-time champs *Paris Saint-Germain* aim to become just the 3rd club ever to win 3 straight titles.

slides.label: The contenders
slides.text: Arsenal, Man City, Liverpool, Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich are all chasing PSG.

slides.label: The final
slides.text: All roads lead to June 5, 2027 at the *Metropolitano Stadium* in Madrid, Spain.

slides.label: How to watch
slides.text: *Paramount+* streams every Champions League match in the US through the 2029/30 season.

slides.label: TV options
slides.text: Some matches also air on *CBS* or CBS Sports Network, both streamable live on Fubo.

slides.label: Matchday 5
slides.text: Nov 24 to 25 features *Arsenal vs Dortmund*, Man City vs Napoli and PSG vs Roma.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: More *live access* to top soccer means more scouting eyes on emerging talent from underrepresented communities worldwide.

caption_instagram:
The Champions League live stream schedule for 2026/27 is here, and Paris Saint-Germain are chasing a historic three-peat in Europe's biggest club competition.

Every match streams on Paramount+ in the US through the 2029/30 season, with select games also airing on CBS and CBS Sports Network via Fubo. The final lands June 5, 2027 at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, where PSG will try to hold off Arsenal, Man City, Liverpool, Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

Matchday 5 runs Nov 24 to 25 with Arsenal vs Dortmund, Man City vs Napoli and PSG vs Roma among the headline games.

Can PSG actually pull off three straight European titles? One word.

caption_linkedin:
The Champions League 2026/27 season continues with a notable media story: CBS and Paramount+ hold exclusive US streaming rights through the 2029/30 season, streaming every single match live.

That's a long-term bet on soccer's growing US audience, and it says something about where media investment is heading. For founders and operators building in sports media, streaming, or content distribution, deals like this are worth studying: multi-year exclusivity, a hybrid free and paid model (CBS Sports Golazo Network remains free to air), and cross-platform access through services like Fubo.

On the field, Paris Saint-Germain are chasing a three-peat, something only two other clubs in Champions League history have done. The final is set for June 5, 2027 at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

What's the smartest long-term media rights move you've seen in sports? Name one.
